title: Dynamic Canary Scheduler with Qualitative Evaluation Hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Enable a small-batch, dynamically adjusted canary scheduler that ties traffic allocation to both quantitative SLOs and a lightweight qualitative evaluation hookset. Goal: reduce time-to-confidence for model rollouts while lowering blast-radius and operational overhead. This ticket scopes the PM and product-facing design: scheduling policy, evaluation hook definition, UI knobs for operators, and acceptance criteria. Engineering tickets will follow to implement runtime enforcement, metrics ingestion, and the CTA in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Can configure a canary campaign with dynamic traffic ramping policy: initial allocation, evaluation interval, and max allocation cap
Evaluation hooks can import a small curated prompt set and produce pass/fail flags for human-reviewable quality checks
Console surfaces live canary state: current allocation, last-eval results, and explicit recommend-next-step (advance/hold/rollback)
Automated stop/rollback triggers for latency and error SLO breaches defined and enforced at runtime
Owners can opt-in to manual override which pauses automated ramping and flags for a human decision
plan: Draft JSON schema for canary policy and eval hooks and review with Eng and Design
Define default conservative policies (e.g., start 1% -> double every 30m while passing checks) and failure thresholds
Design Console UX: canary creation flow, live timeline, and quick rollback CTA
Pilot with internal non-critical model routing to validate signal quality and human-review latency
Iterate on thresholds after one pilot cycle, then prepare a limited public beta for selected customers
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design & schema review (this ticket) - produce spec and mockups
Phase 1: Internal pilot - route <5% traffic, 4 eval windows, require human sign-off to reach >25%
Phase 2: Beta - selected customers, enable automated rollback by default, track false positive rate of eval hooks
Phase 3: General availability - default conservative policy, opt-out for advanced customers
Rollback criteria: sustained latency >150% baseline for 3 consecutive eval windows OR quality regression >5% on core prompt set
metrics: Token-level latency p50/p95 during canary windows
Request error rate and 5xxs from backend
Delta in core quality score across curated prompt set (automated eval)
Time-to-decision for human review actions during pilot

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives from automated eval hooks could unnecessarily halt rollouts. Mitigation: require 2-of-3 failing windows before auto-stop during beta.
Risk: Human review latency delays rollout progression. Mitigation: provide clear triage queues and SLAs for internal pilot; escalate via Ops playbook
Risk: Metric noise for low-volume canaries. Mitigation: limit dynamic automation to campaigns with min traffic or aggregate across windows
Risk: Complexity in runtime routing. Mitigation: implement labels and lightweight routing policy first, defer advanced scheduling to follow-up
notes: Keep initial rollout conservative to build trust in automated gating. The goal is faster confidence, not faster rollouts at the cost of stability.
Coordinate with privacy/compliance if curated prompt sets include customer PII. Flagged for legal review if needed.
Post-pilot retrospective will capture false-positive rate, operator burden, and any required metric additions. Schedule retrospective in Cycle 2025-W42.
